title: Score of a String
statement: For every pair of neighbouring characters in the string `s`, take the absolute value of the difference between their ASCII codes. The **score** of `s` is the total of these values over all neighbouring pairs. Return the score of `s`.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The score only looks at characters that sit next to each other, so a single left-to-right pass is enough: for each position after the first, compare the character with the one just before it and add the size of the gap between their codes.

## Approach

1. Start `score` at 0.
2. For each index `i` from 1 to the end, read the codes `previous` (at `i - 1`) and `current` (at `i`).
3. Add `Math.abs(current - previous)` to `score`.
4. Return `score`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "hello"` has codes `h = 104`, `e = 101`, `l = 108`, `l = 108`, `o = 111`.

- `i = 1`: `|101 - 104| = 3`, `score = 3`.
- `i = 2`: `|108 - 101| = 7`, `score = 10`.
- `i = 3`: `|108 - 108| = 0`, `score = 10`.
- `i = 4`: `|111 - 108| = 3`, `score = 13`.

The answer is `13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the string.
- Space: O(1): two codes and a running total.

## Pitfalls

- Start the loop at 1 (or stop one early) so `i - 1` never falls outside the string.
- Take the absolute value: going down the alphabet (`z` to `a`) adds 25, not -25.
- Equal neighbours contribute 0, which is fine; do not skip them in a way that misaligns the pairs.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `score` | running total of the gaps |
| `i` | index of the right character in the current pair |
| `previous`, `current` | ASCII codes of `s[i - 1]` and `s[i]` |

narration.3: Each index from 1 onward forms a pair with the character before it.
narration.4: Read the code of the left character of the pair.
narration.5: Read the code of the right character of the pair.
narration.6: Add the size of the gap, ignoring its direction.
narration.8: Every neighbouring pair has been counted; return the total.
